page: Microsoft Azure E32-8s_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz with 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, delivering 8 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration includes 256.0 GB of RAM, which provides a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per core. It is equipped with 524 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage, but does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data shows a clear contrast between CPU compute and memory performance. Single-core CPU performance, single-threaded compression, and text processing benchmarks fall into the bottom 25% tier. However, multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth tests, including read-only and write operations on large blocks, consistently perform in the average tier. Database operations and Redis SET operations, achieving 6.41 million operations per second, also register in the average tier, indicating stable transactional capabilities despite the weaker raw single-core compute.

The primary tradeoff of the E32-8s_v3 is its low compute-to-memory ratio, where CPU-heavy tasks like LLM inference and ray tracing perform poorly, but memory-intensive workloads benefit from the massive 256 GB RAM allocation. From a cost-efficiency perspective, this server is optimized for workloads requiring high memory density rather than raw processing power. It is best suited for memory-intensive applications, database caching, and enterprise database operations that fit within its memory footprint but do not require high-frequency CPU performance.
description: Microsoft Azure E32-8s_v3 is an x86_64 memory-optimized server from the ESv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 256.0 GB of RAM, and 524 GB of local storage. While single-core CPU performance and text processing benchmarks are weak, falling in the bottom 25% tier, the server delivers average multi-core performance and memory bandwidth. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the average tier, with Redis reaching 6.41 million operations per second. Lacking GPU acceleration, this server presents a clear tradeoff: it offers massive memory capacity at the expense of high-performance compute. It is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, enterprise database operations, and caching systems that require substantial memory density rather than intensive CPU processing.
